note: v218 / ADR 0029 — THE GENERAL LISTENER. ADR 0028's recorder is FOCUSED: it is handed a domain and records the answer to the question that was asked, and the 2026-08-25 adversarial audit explicitly REFUSED to repeal that restriction — 'something else in the same breath never excuses the domain's own answer' is what keeps a mission abroad from being filed as military service. But people say datable things when nobody asked. These cases drive `landmark_recorder.listen_to_answer` — the same loop with `domain=None` — and pin the mode's whole contract: typed lists (`landmarks` any domain, `people` FAMILY-ONLY by owner ruling), a deterministic prescreen, and the backstop that makes it shippable. Deliberately NOT in landmark_fixtures.json: these are listener completions, not reference transcripts.

cases.note: The founder shape the whole mode exists for: nobody asked a landmark question, and one sentence carries a move, a school and a job. Three records, three domains, one attempt, no lint. The FOCUSED recorder could not have produced two of these — its restriction to the asked domain is a property of focused mode and is untouched.
cases.user_message: We moved to Dayton in 1974, right after I finished at Fairview High, and I started at Danforth Steel that fall.
cases.reply: Dayton in '74 — and straight into the steel.

cases.note: The asymmetry, pinned. The prescreen is LIBERAL by owner ruling, so it fires on messages that carry no fact — here it does not fire at all and the listener's honest empty answer is simply correct. A prescreen false positive is never a listener failure: see `listener_heard_nothing`, where the lint fires on prescreen-positive + both lists empty + no decline, and the noise costs exactly one haiku-class regeneration.
cases.user_message: I love a good pizza and a long walk, and not much else.

cases.note: The v217 seam, reached by ear. A sibling's birth year is a FAMILY person date, so it becomes a roster entry through `entity-verdict --born` with the basis travelling beside it — not a landmark record, because `family`'s own ladder is not what was asked here.
cases.user_message: My sister Ruth was born in 1948, two years before me.

cases.note: The owner's ruling, enforced where a prompt cannot be talked out of it. The listener heard a dated person and `validate_person_record` refused the record because a colleague is not family — a NAMED drop (`person_relation_not_family`), never a silent one. It also clears the backstop: a refusal is a decision, not a miss, and regenerating would ask the model to break the rule it just obeyed.
cases.user_message: My old boss Hal was born in 1948 — he ran that shop for thirty years.
cases.reply: Hal ran it a long time.

cases.note: v216's dedupe holds in the no-focus mode. Two children are already filed with their exact birthdays; the person goes back over them and there is nothing new in it. The listener files nothing in ONE attempt — the backstop does not fire, because every fragment the prescreen saw is already in the store word for word (`store_terms`), which is the one place where 'was this fragment consumed?' is decidable.
cases.user_message: Corinne was born 2 April 1979 and Maddox 15 November 1981.

cases.note: The non-negotiable, and the reason the mode can ship at all. ADR 0028 certified that prompt prose alone is ignorable, so the no-focus mode ships with its own deterministic backstop: the prescreen saw a year, the listener came back with nothing twice, and the outcome is WITHHELD carrying `landmark_gates.listener_heard_nothing` — a state a host sweep can run again. Never silence, and never a fabricated record. Exactly `answer_must_record`'s shape.
cases.user_message: We moved to Dayton in 1974 and the whole street smelled of the mill.

cases.note: ADR 0028 amendment §2, carried in: each record runs BOTH pinned validators ALONE, so a record naming a key its domain cannot read drops by itself and never takes a sibling with it. `birth` is not a key `family` can read (it degrades the whole record to None) and `pets` is not a domain at all; the move survives both.
cases.user_message: We moved to Dayton in 1974 and my brother James was born in 1962.
